title: Optimizing Recovery Logic in Speculative High-Level Synthesis
problem: Speculative HLS introduces significant area overhead from rollback control logic when handling kernels with complex, irregular control-flow, offsetting throughput gains.
motivation: Speculative scheduling can expose parallelism in irregular control-flow kernels, but the rollback logic required for incorrect predictions becomes prohibitively expensive.
method: The approach uses static analysis to examine code structure and determine which speculative execution paths require rollback capability—the circuits that undo work when the hardware's guess was wrong. It then applies linear programming, a mathematical optimization technique, to eliminate unnecessary control logic, keeping only the circuitry needed for actual rollback in complex control flow.
key_novelty: First work combining static analysis with linear programming to systematically reduce the hardware area overhead from rollback control logic in speculative synthesis.
contributions: Simplification/elimination of rollback control logic via static analysis
LP-based optimization of recovery logic structure
Improvements in both execution throughput and area cost

metrics.other: throughput improvement, area cost reduction (values not specified)

baselines: traditional static scheduling, speculative scheduling without optimization
limitations: Not discussed; specific metrics not provided; applicability to specific kernel types unclear.
